LPL Financial Brings In $2.035 Billion In Combined Client Assets Represented By Four Joining Practices
By Amit Chowdhry
Yesterday at 4:03 PM
LPL Financial Brings In $2.035 Billion In Combined Client Assets Represented By Four Joining Practices
LPL Financial has welcomed four wealth management practices reporting approximately $2.035 billion in combined client assets, expanding its advisor network through affiliations announced over the last couple of days. SteadRock Private Wealth, FHT Advisors, Impel Wealth Management and Sound Foundation Wealth Advisors joined LPL’s broker-dealer and Registered Investment Advisor platforms. The reported assets include advisory, brokerage and retirement plan assets.
SteadRock Private Wealth
Nathan J. “Nate” Hershman joined LPL from Edward Jones to launch SteadRock Private Wealth in North Canton, Ohio. He reported serving approximately $185 million in advisory, brokerage and retirement plan assets.
SteadRock serves families, individuals approaching or living in retirement, and business owners, including those in manufacturing. Its planning approach connects investments and retirement needs with business interests, charitable priorities and financial legacies.
For business owners, planning can include preparing for a transition and evaluating how a sale or succession could affect retirement and family objectives. Hershman selected LPL to establish an independent practice with access to its technology, investment platform and business support.
FHT Advisors
FHT Advisors joined LPL from Cetera alongside Impel Wealth Management. The two Ohio-based practices reported approximately $1.15 billion in combined client assets and will retain their separate identities.
Led by Brian Toma, FHT serves clients across 32 states, including professionals, medical professionals, younger families, people approaching retirement and retirees.
The firm operates as an ensemble practice, bringing multiple advisors’ experience and planning perspectives to client relationships. Its advisory team includes Sarah Stewart, Tom Drager, Tammy Hafner, Bruce Baker, Bear Rupert, Jonathan Goldston, Seann Schaller and financial consultant Stephen Ehrhardt.
FHT identified LPL’s technology, planning capabilities and resources as factors supporting its next stage of development.
Impel Wealth Management
Jesse Hurst leads Impel Wealth Management, which began by serving corporate executives around Akron and has expanded into multigenerational wealth management.
Hurst works alongside advisors Nathan Ollish and Irene Zurowski. Ollish serves many next-generation clients, while Zurowski’s focus includes retirement plans and female executives.
Impel works with dozens of families across at least two generations and more than a dozen across three generations. The team also produces market and financial planning commentary through recurring blog posts and videos.
Hurst and FHT’s Toma have worked alongside one another for 25 years, exchanging ideas and best practices while independently leading their firms. Impel selected LPL for its technology, advanced planning resources and growth opportunities.
Sound Foundation Wealth Advisors
Sound Foundation Wealth Advisors joined from Cambridge Investment Research Advisors, reporting approximately $700 million in advisory, brokerage and retirement plan assets.

India's artificial intelligence (AI) startup ecosystem has attracted approximately $1.91 billion across 102 funding rounds between January 1 and November 5, 2026, with a handful of large-ticket transactions accounting for a significant portion of the capital raised, according to data compiled by Tracxn .
The funding activity includes investments across companies developing AI infrastructure, generative AI platforms and enterprise applications, with some of the largest transactions involving businesses operating in the infrastructure and computing ecosystem.
Advt
Neysa's $600 million Series B round in February was the largest funding transaction recorded during the period. Sarvam followed with a $255.1 million Series B round in June, while semiconductor technology company Kandou raised $225 million through a Series E round in March.
Other significant transactions included Yotta's $150 million Series D round in July and Emergent's $130 million Series C round in the same month. Emergent had also raised $70 million through a Series B round in January.
Sarvam subsequently raised another $90.4 million in August, while Freehand secured $75 million through a Series B round in July.
The four largest funding transactions — involving Neysa, Sarvam, Kandou and Yotta — together accounted for approximately $1.23 billion, or nearly 64 per cent of the total funding recorded during the period.
Peak XV Partners leads investor participation
Sarvam subsequently raised another $90.4 million in August, while Freehand secured $75 million through a Series B round in July. On the investor side, Peak XV Partners emerged as the most active investor in India's AI startup funding landscape, participating in six funding rounds during the period.
Khosla Ventures, Lightspeed Venture Partners, Together, Info Edge Ventures, Capital 2B, IvyCap Ventures, Antler, Venture Catalysts and Wyser followed, with participation in three rounds each.
Advt
In terms of lead-investor participation, Peak XV Partners led three funding rounds, while IvyCap Ventures and Info Edge Ventures led two rounds each.
The investor activity reflects participation by established venture capital firms, as well as funds backing emerging AI companies at different stages of development.
The funding rounds recorded during the period included seed, Series A, Series B, and later-stage investments, as well as venture debt, conventional debt, and grant-related entries.

The energy producer also raised the midpoint of its full-year adjusted operating earnings guidance while advancing major nuclear power agreements with Amazon and Google.

articles.text:
Constellation Energy: $1.8 Billion Q3 Net Income, Raised 2026 Guidance, And $5 Billion Nuclear Financing Commitment
By Amit Chowdhry
Today at 3:01 AM
Constellation Energy: $1.8 Billion Q3 Net Income, Raised 2026 Guidance, And $5 Billion Nuclear Financing Commitment
Constellation Energy Corporation reported third-quarter 2026 net income of $1.835 billion, compared with $930 million a year earlier, as the company benefited from favorable market conditions and the addition of Calpine. The energy producer also raised the midpoint of its full-year adjusted operating earnings guidance while advancing major nuclear power agreements with Amazon and Google.
For the quarter ended September 30, 2026, Constellation reported GAAP earnings of $5.19 per share, compared with $2.97 in the prior-year period. Adjusted operating earnings increased to $1.792 billion, or $5.06 per share, from $952 million, or $3.04 per share, a year earlier.
The company narrowed its full-year adjusted operating earnings guidance to $12.50 to $12.80 per share, raising the midpoint for the second time in 2026.
Constellation attributed its quarterly performance primarily to favorable market and portfolio conditions and the addition of Calpine, which it acquired in January 2026. Higher interest costs and unfavorable nuclear production tax credit portfolio effects partially offset those benefits.
Beyond its financial results, Constellation highlighted several agreements intended to expand electricity generation capacity and support growing demand from technology companies and other large energy customers.
In September, Constellation announced a 20-year, 690-megawatt power purchase agreement with Amazon, along with a related retail supply agreement supporting Amazon’s operations in the PJM electricity market. The arrangement will enable more than $3 billion in infrastructure investments at the Calvert Cliffs Clean Energy Center, including facility improvements and a 190-megawatt capacity expansion expected between 2030 and 2032.
In October, Constellation announced a separate 20-year power purchase agreement with Google supporting more than $4.3 billion in investments across 11 nuclear generating units in Illinois, Pennsylvania, and New Jersey.
The Google agreement is expected to add approximately 890 megawatts of incremental nuclear generation capacity to the PJM grid, with the first uprate scheduled for 2028. Constellation also entered into a 15-year financial energy load-following agreement with Google covering 2,700 megawatts.
Together, the Amazon and Google arrangements support more than 1,000 megawatts of additional nuclear generating capacity.
Constellation also signed a conditional loan commitment with the U.S. Department of Energy for up to $5 billion to finance nuclear uprates. Subject to execution of a final loan agreement, the financing would involve a 30-year loan from the Federal Financing Bank, backed by a federal guarantee.
The company additionally agreed to acquire the Rhode Island State Energy Center from Shell Energy North America for $715 million, subject to customary adjustments and regulatory approvals. The 609-megawatt natural gas-fired facility operates in the ISO New England wholesale electricity market and would become part of Constellation’s merchant generation portfolio.

articles.title: Pfizer: Up To $1.5 Billion Funding Agreement With Blackstone Life Sciences To Advance Monthly GLP-1 Obesity Drug
articles.snippet:
Pfizer and Blackstone Life Sciences have entered into a strategic funding agreement under which funds managed by Blackstone will provide up to $1.5 billion through 2028 to support the clinical development of berobenatide, Pfizer's investigational monthly GLP-1 receptor agonist for chronic weight management and obesity-related conditions.
The post Pfizer: Up To $1.5 Billion Funding Agreement With Blackstone Life Sciences To Advance Monthly GLP-1 Obesity Drug appeared first on Pulse 2.0 .
articles.text:
Pfizer: Up To $1.5 Billion Funding Agreement With Blackstone Life Sciences To Advance Monthly GLP-1 Obesity Drug
By Amit Chowdhry
Today at 2:21 PM
Pfizer: Up To $1.5 Billion Funding Agreement With Blackstone Life Sciences To Advance Monthly GLP-1 Obesity Drug
Pfizer and Blackstone Life Sciences have entered into a strategic funding agreement under which funds managed by Blackstone will provide up to $1.5 billion through 2028 to support the clinical development of berobenatide, Pfizer’s investigational monthly GLP-1 receptor agonist for chronic weight management and obesity-related conditions.
The agreement will help Pfizer advance its obesity drug development program while maintaining financial flexibility to invest in other therapeutic areas. In exchange for its funding commitment, Blackstone will become eligible for milestone-based payments tied to U.S. regulatory approval and commercial performance.
Berobenatide is being developed as a potential first-in-class monthly injectable GLP-1 receptor agonist peptide. Pfizer is evaluating the treatment for chronic weight management and obesity-related conditions, including knee osteoarthritis and obstructive sleep apnea.
The transaction represents a significant investment in Pfizer’s cardiometabolic pipeline as the pharmaceutical company advances a broad portfolio of investigational obesity therapies.
How The $1.5 Billion Funding Agreement Works
Under the agreement, Blackstone-managed funds will cover up to $1.5 billion in development expenses associated with berobenatide through 2028.
In return, Blackstone will be eligible to receive payments if the drug achieves specified regulatory and commercial milestones.
These payments are contingent on U.S. regulatory approval of monthly injectable berobenatide monotherapy for chronic weight management and the achievement of certain sales targets.
Any milestone payments earned by Blackstone would be distributed over multiple years.
The structure allows Pfizer to obtain external funding for a major clinical development program without selling ownership or commercial rights to the investigational medicine.
Pfizer will retain full operational control and decision-making authority over berobenatide, including its clinical development strategy.
The agreement also does not provide Blackstone with an ownership interest in the drug.
Funds managed by Blackstone’s perpetual private equity strategy, BXPE, will participate alongside funds managed by Blackstone Life Sciences.
The arrangement illustrates an alternative approach to financing pharmaceutical research, in which investment firms provide capital to support clinical development in exchange for payments linked to future milestones.
For Pfizer, the agreement provides an opportunity to share development costs while retaining control over a potentially important pipeline asset.
Berobenatide Targets Monthly GLP-1 Treatment
Berobenatide is an investigational GLP-1 receptor agonist peptide being studied for chronic weight management and related medical conditions.
GLP-1 receptor agonists act on biological pathways involved in appetite regulation, blood glucose control, and other metabolic processes.
Existing treatments in this drug class have established a significant market for obesity and metabolic disease therapies.
Pfizer is developing berobenatide as a potential monthly injectable treatment, which could offer a different administration schedule from therapies requiring more frequent dosing.

articles.text:
Rowan Digital Infrastructure: $1.5 Billion In New Financing To Accelerate 5.5 GW Hyperscale Data Center Pipeline
By Amit Chowdhry
Yesterday at 3:43 PM
Rowan Digital Infrastructure: $1.5 Billion In New Financing To Accelerate 5.5 GW Hyperscale Data Center Pipeline
Rowan Digital Infrastructure, a Denver-based developer of hyperscale data center campuses, has secured more than $1.5 billion in new corporate financing capacity to accelerate development of its 5.5-gigawatt project pipeline across the United States. The financing includes a $600 million expansion of its holding company term loan led by Apterra Infrastructure Capital, along with a new $590 million revolving credit facility and a $355 million letter of credit facility led by Citibank.
The transactions provide Rowan with additional financing flexibility to secure land, obtain power commitments, purchase equipment, and advance early-stage development activities across its portfolio of hyperscale data center projects.
With the latest transactions, Rowan has secured more than $8 billion in financing from over 40 lenders during the past 18 months.
The company’s development pipeline includes multiple large-scale data center campuses designed to support major technology companies and hyperscale computing operators.
Rowan has already contracted more than 1.2 gigawatts of capacity with major technology customers.
The additional corporate financing is intended to help the company accelerate the development of new facilities while maintaining access to capital across multiple projects.
$600 Million Term Loan Expansion
Rowan expanded its existing holding company credit facility by $600 million, increasing the total facility size to $900 million.
The original $300 million facility was established in September 2025 to support early-stage development activities.
Apterra Infrastructure Capital served as lead arranger for the expanded financing.
The additional term loan capacity provides Rowan with resources to support project development before individual campuses reach the construction financing stage.
These activities can include land acquisition, infrastructure planning, engineering, permitting, and coordination with electricity providers.
Early-stage financing is particularly important in hyperscale data center development because projects can require significant capital commitments before construction begins.
Rowan’s expanded corporate facility allows the company to pursue additional opportunities while progressing existing projects through development.
New $945 Million Credit Facilities Led By Citibank
In addition to the term loan expansion, Rowan established two new corporate credit facilities totaling $945 million.
The financing consists of a $590 million revolving credit facility and a $355 million letter of credit facility.
Citibank served as lead left arranger and administrative agent for both facilities.
The revolving credit arrangement provides Rowan with access to liquidity that can be borrowed, repaid, and borrowed again as its project pipeline develops.
This structure is intended to reduce the need for the company to obtain separate financing for every new development site.
The letter of credit facility provides financial support for obligations associated with project development.
These can include utility interconnection deposits, equipment vendor commitments, and other collateral requirements.

articles.title: Whitecap Resources raises 2026 production guidance and dividend after posting record Q3 funds flow of $1.2 billion
articles.snippet: Whitecap Resources raises 2026 production guidance and dividend after posting record Q3 funds flow of $1.2 billion Energies Media
articles.text:
Oil & Gas
Whitecap Resources raises 2026 production guidance and dividend after posting record Q3 funds flow of $1.2 billion
By Kelly Lippke · November 15, 2026 · 8:45 AM · 5 min read
Written by Kelly Lippke
Calgary-based Whitecap Resources (TSX: WCP) posted Q3 2026 funds flow of $888 million USD (CAD 1.2 billion) — a company record, and a 32% per-share jump from the same quarter a year ago . Production averaged 390,720 boe/d, beating internal forecasts for the period.
Off the back of those results, Whitecap’s board raised full-year 2026 production guidance to 392,000 boe/d — the third upward revision of the year. They also bumped the monthly dividend about 1.5% to $0.046 USD ($0.0617 CAD) per share and approved a 2027 capital budget of $1.78–$1.92 billion USD (CAD 2.4–2.6 billion), targeting average output of 400,000–410,000 boe/d.
Q3 2026 production and financial results
Whitecap’s Q3 2026 output of 390,720 boe/d — 61% liquids — cleared internal forecasts and improved on the 374,623 boe/d from Q3 2025. Funds flow hit $866 million USD (CAD 1.17 billion) , or $0.71 USD ($0.96 CAD) per diluted share, a 32% per-share increase year-over-year. The headline number was strong, and the underlying details held up just as well.
The board raised the monthly dividend about 1.5% to $0.046 USD ($0.0617 CAD) per share, or $0.55 USD ($0.74 CAD) annualized, starting with the November 2026 payment.
Free funds flow reached $474 million USD (CAD 640 million) after $394 million USD (CAD 533 million) in capital expenditures. Through the first nine months of 2026, free funds flow totaled $1.41 billion USD (CAD 1.9 billion) — a solid cash generation pace for a company actively investing in growth.
Net income came in at $241 million USD (CAD 326 million), or $0.20 USD ($0.27 CAD) per share. A non-cash unrealized loss of roughly $222 million USD (CAD 300 million) on commodity contracts — driven by rising forward prices during the quarter — held that figure back. Stripping out that accounting item leaves an even cleaner underlying operating picture.
Drivers behind the outperformance
Several factors pushed production above forecast. Strong base and new well performance at Gold Creek and Kaybob Duvernay, combined with solid output from the Conventional division, moved volumes above plan. Higher light oil and condensate prices lifted realized revenues significantly — crude oil and condensate averaged $84.28 USD ($113.89 CAD) per barrel in Q3 2026, compared to $62.41 USD ($84.34 CAD) per barrel in Q3 2025.
Faster capital cycle times allowed Whitecap to run its drilling program ahead of schedule , and that efficiency showed up directly in per-boe operating costs: $7.56 USD ($10.22 CAD) in Q3 2026, down from $8.79 USD ($11.88 CAD) in Q2 2026.
